$comment: Verified citations. Every quote byte-matches its pinned source (`python tools/cite.py --check`). That a quote EXISTS is mechanical; that it ESTABLISHES its element is a human judgment recorded in PROVENANCE.md. See the SUPERSEDED entry: a real passage can be real and expired.

citations.quote: An OPO must have a written agreement with 95 percent of the Medicare and Medicaid participating hospitals and critical access hospitals in its service area that have both a ventilator and an operating room and have not been granted a waiver by CMS to work with another OPO.
citations.establishes: The OPO-hospital referral relationship is a written agreement the OPO must hold, at a stated coverage threshold of its service area.

citations.quote: The agreement must specify the meaning of the terms “timely referral” and “imminent death.”
citations.establishes: 'Timely referral' is DEFINED IN THE AGREEMENT and not federally. The response bound is per-hospital, not national.

citations.quote: An OPO is evaluated by measuring the donation rate and the organ transplantation rate in their DSA.
citations.establishes: TWO outcome measures, codified. Confirms the fact-sheet claim against the regulation itself.
citations.currency_confirmed: 486.318(a)(4) scopes the sunset to (a)(1)-(3) only; this quote is from paragraph (d), which carries no sunset and is the regime in force. Confirmed against the full section 2026-08-26.

citations.quote: The donation rate is calculated as the number of donors in the DSA as a percentage of the donor potential.
citations.establishes: Numerator: donors in the DSA. Denominator: donor potential.
citations.currency_confirmed: 486.318(a)(4) scopes the sunset to (a)(1)-(3) only; this quote is from paragraph (d), which carries no sunset and is the regime in force. Confirmed against the full section 2026-08-26.

citations.quote: The organ transplantation rate is calculated as the number of organs transplanted from donors in the DSA as a percentage of the donor potential.
citations.establishes: Numerator: organs transplanted from DSA donors. Denominator: the same donor potential.
citations.currency_confirmed: 486.318(a)(4) scopes the sunset to (a)(1)-(3) only; this quote is from paragraph (d), which carries no sunset and is the regime in force. Confirmed against the full section 2026-08-26.

citations.quote: The denominator for the outcome measures is the donor potential and is based on inpatient deaths within the DSA from patients 75 or younger with a primary cause of death that is consistent with organ donation.
citations.establishes: The denominator is far more specific than 'inpatient death records': patients 75 or younger, primary cause consistent with organ donation, from state death certificates, most recent 12 months.
citations.currency_confirmed: 486.318(a)(4) scopes the sunset to (a)(1)-(3) only; this quote is from paragraph (d), which carries no sunset and is the regime in force. Confirmed against the full section 2026-08-26.

citations.quote: Tier 3—OPOs that have an upper limit of the one-sided 95 percent confidence interval for their donation or organ transplantation rates that are below the median threshold rate established for their DSA will be identified at each assessment period.
citations.establishes: Tier 3 is triggered by falling below median on donation OR transplantation - either measure, not both. Tiers are computed per DSA.
citations.currency_confirmed: 486.318(a)(4) scopes the sunset to (a)(1)-(3) only; this quote is from paragraph (d), which carries no sunset and is the regime in force. Confirmed against the full section 2026-08-26.

citations.quote: Verify that death has been pronounced according to applicable local, State, and Federal laws.
citations.establishes: The OPO's duty is to VERIFY a pronouncement made elsewhere. It does not pronounce. Stronger and more precise than the drafted claim of 'separation of functions'.

citations.quote: Data reported by the OPO to the OPTN must be reported within 30 days after the end of the month in which a death occurred.
citations.establishes: A REAL federal deadline with a number - unlike t_referral_response. This one is genuinely L0.

citations.quote: If an OPO determines through death record review or other means that the data it reported to the OPTN was incorrect, it must report the corrected data to the OPTN within 30 days of the end of the month in which the error is identified.
citations.establishes: Corrections are REPORTED, not erased - the regulation itself is append-with-correction, which is the tape's design.

citations.quote: The outcome measures described in § 486.318(a)(1) through (3) are effective until July 31, 2022.
citations.establishes: RECORDED AS A NEAR-MISS. 486.318(a)-(c) describes an expired three-measure regime and is still in the codified text. A search hit on 'outcome measures' lands there first. The byte-match gate would PASS a citation to it, because the passage is real - it is merely no longer in force. This is the limit of the mechanical gate, demonstrated rather than asserted.
citations.currency_confirmed: NOT in force — retained deliberately as the recorded near-miss. This is the expired regime, kept so the failure mode stays visible.

citations.quote: Ensure that the potential donor's blood is typed using two separate blood samples.
citations.establishes: Donor typing must use TWO separate samples - a duplication requirement, not a single test.

citations.quote: Document potential donor's record with all test results, including blood type, before organ recovery.
citations.establishes: Testing completeness is a GUARD on recovery: results must be in the record BEFORE recovery, which is exactly a transition guard.

citations.quote: An OPTN member procuring an organ shall operate the OPTN computer match program within such time as the OPTN may prescribe to identify and rank potential recipients for each cadaveric organ procured.
citations.establishes: Ranking is performed by the OPTN computer match program. The OPO operates it; it does not rank.

citations.quote: An organ offer is made when all information necessary to determine whether to transplant the organ into the potential recipient has been given to the transplant hospital.
citations.establishes: An offer is DEFINED BY COMPLETENESS of information transferred - not by a message being sent. A completeness condition, precisely the class the gates check.

citations.quote: The OPTN member that is transporting an organ shall assure that it is accompanied by written documentation of activities conducted to determine the suitability of the organ donor and shall maintain this document for one year.
citations.establishes: Documentation travels WITH the organ, and is retained one year. The record is a conserved artifact, not a database row.

citations.quote: All OPOs and transplant programs shall maintain such records pertaining to each potential donor identified, each organ retrieved, each recipient transplanted and such other transplantation-related matters as the Secretary deems necessary to carry out her/his responsibilities under the Act.
citations.establishes: Records are required for EACH POTENTIAL DONOR IDENTIFIED - not only converted cases. The non-conversion terminals in the lifecycle are therefore mandated record-keeping, not a design nicety.

citations.quote: Attempt to obtain the deceased donor’s medical and behavioral history from one or more individuals familiar with the donor according to Policy 2.4: Deceased Donor Medical and Behavioral History, to screen for medical conditions that may affect the decision to use the donated organ.
citations.establishes: Screening is a defined four-step duty. Note step 4: if information is unavailable, the ABSENCE and its reason must be documented — an absence is a required record, not a blank.

citations.quote: Document in the deceased donor medical record if any of this information is not available and the reason it is not available.
citations.establishes: MISSING INFORMATION IS ITSELF A REQUIRED ENTRY. The policy mandates recording an absence with its reason - which is the ledger-of-silence property, already required by rule.

citations.quote: The host OPO must make reasonable efforts to manage the deceased donor by addressing all of the following: 1. Maintaining blood pressure for perfusion of vital organs 2. Monitoring vital signs 3. Administering IV therapy or drugs, as required 4. Administering antibiotic therapy, as required 5. Administering and monitoring fluid intake and output
citations.establishes: Five enumerated management duties, with documentation and reporting required. The standard is 'reasonable efforts', not an outcome.

citations.quote: The host OPO may only recover organs that it has received authorization to recover.
citations.establishes: Authorization is a hard precondition on recovery, per organ. Exactly a transition guard.

citations.quote: If an authorized organ is not recovered, the host OPO must document the specific reason for non-recovery.
citations.establishes: Non-recovery requires a documented SPECIFIC REASON. The non-conversion terminal is a mandated record with a required reason code.

citations.quote: The donor hospital healthcare team member who declares the death of the potential deceased donor cannot be involved in any aspect of the organ recovery procedure or transplantation of that donor’s organs.
citations.establishes: SEPARATION OF FUNCTIONS, explicitly. The declarer may not participate in recovery or transplantation. This is the claim originally drafted for this element and not found in the CFR - it is here.

citations.quote: 2.15 Requirements for Controlled Donation after Circulatory Death
citations.establishes: Controlled DCD is a distinct pathway with its own protocol, evaluation, consent, authorization, withdrawal, pronouncement and recovery requirements (2.15.A-I).

citations.quote: The host OPO is responsible for follow up and reporting of deceased donor test results received after procurement.
citations.establishes: Disposition does not close the case: results arriving AFTER procurement must still be obtained and reported. The record stays open to late-arriving truth.

citations.quote: Host OPOs must develop and comply with a written protocol to perform a pre-recovery verification for each organ recovered as required below.
citations.establishes: A written pre-recovery verification protocol is required, PER ORGAN, before recovery.

citations.quote: Qualified health care professionals, as defined in the host OPO’s protocol, must perform all verifications. At least one of the individuals performing a verification must be an OPO staff member.
citations.establishes: Verification is TWO-PERSON, at least one of whom is OPO staff - a four-eyes requirement, and the definition of 'qualified' is delegated to the OPO's own protocol (an L2 variation point).
